latin: Si teneatur communis uia quod actu intellectus attingatur deus, dico duas sequentes conclusiones, quarum haec est prima: quod uidentes uerbum, eo actu quo essentiam diuinam attingunt, creaturas non attingunt nisi eminenter, equipollenter ad formalem cognitionem, equipollentia non actus sed obiecti.
translation: Granting the common view that God is reached by an act of intellect, I put forward two conclusions, the first being this: those who see the Word attain created things, by that same act by which they attain the divine essence, only in an elevated manner equivalent to formal knowledge of them — an equivalence of object, not of act.
translation_note: Argued conditionally from within the 'common view' Pico elsewhere departs from (cf. 3>43); paired with 4>12 as its second conclusion.
